sections.h2: Where are the Mason County tax offices in Maysville?
sections.html:
All three offices are in Maysville. One sets the value, one collects this year's bill, and the third records deeds and inherits any bill that stays unpaid.

  • PVA: 220 1/2 Sutton Street, (606) 564-3700, staffed through the workweek. It handles value, mailing and property addresses, and exemptions.
  • Sheriff: 120 West Third Street, in the old Health Department building, 606-564-3309, doors open at nine on weekdays, and a drop box takes checks only.
  • Clerk: 27 West 3rd Street, PO Box 234, (606) 564-3341, opening at eight on weekdays and closing for lunch between 11:30 and 12:30.

Before disputing a bill, know what the PVA controls. Its page says the office writes no laws and sets no rates. Fiscal court members, city officials and school boards vote the rates, so a rate complaint goes to them.

sections.h2: Why does the Ohio River matter to Mason County sellers?
sections.html:
Mason County is a river county in northeastern Kentucky, and the Ohio River marks its northern edge, facing Brown and Adams counties in Ohio. It was created in 1788 from Bourbon County, Virginia, and honors George Mason, a delegate to the Constitutional Convention. It covers 246 square miles, 240 of them land, and adjoins Lewis, Fleming, Robertson and Bracken counties.

Maysville is both seat and largest city. Dover, Germantown and Sardis round out the incorporated places, while Mays Lick is a census-designated place. Helena, Lewisburg, Minerva, Old Washington, Orangeburg and Shannon are unincorporated. Federal statisticians treat Mason County as the Maysville micropolitan area, which rolls up into the Cincinnati-Wilmington-Maysville combined area.

Headcounts tell a long story. Mason County had 12,182 people in 1800, 18,344 in 1850 and 20,773 in 1890. It then dropped to 16,666 by 1990, rebounded to 17,490 in 2010 and eased to 17,120 in 2020. The latest estimate, 16,936, is 1.1 percent under the 2020 base.

Age is spread fairly evenly: 22.5 percent of residents are under 18 and 21.8 percent are 65 or older. Between the 2010 and 2020 censuses the county lost 2.1 percent of its residents. Mason County Schools is the single public district. Its campuses are Mason County High School, Mason County Middle School, Mason County Intermediate School and Straub Elementary School.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers reveal about Mason County households?
sections.html:
Owners live in two of every three homes, and the head count has been slipping.

A typical household brings in $52,178, and per capita income is $31,189. Poverty touches 15.2 percent of residents, and 18.5 percent of those under 65 report a disability. Diplomas are held by 86.3 percent of adults and bachelor's degrees by 20.0 percent. The trip to work takes 26.8 minutes on average. Veterans number 908, and 1,209 businesses employ nobody but their owners. Elbow room is plentiful: 71.3 people per square mile in 2020, slightly under the 72.8 of 2010. The workforce includes 55.4 percent of residents 16 and older, 88.6 percent of residents did not move in the past year, 90.8 percent of households have a computer, and 8.7 percent of residents under 65 are uninsured. Households average 2.34 people. In 2023, 404 employer establishments carried 6,951 workers on a $336.4 million payroll, and employment grew 4.9 percent. The 2022 receipts were $152.4 million in health care and social assistance and $114.2 million in transportation and warehousing, and retail sales totaled $477.4 million, or $28,246 per resident.

sections.h2: What does the sheriff's Taxpayer's Notice say about timing and penalties?
sections.html:
The sheriff's notice sets out four periods, and the bill itself arrives on a yellow postcard.

  • Two percent discount, October 1 to November 1.
  • Face amount, the next two months.
  • Five percent penalty, January only.
  • Twenty-one percent penalty, February to April 15.

The usual timetable is set out in KRS 134.015. The sheriff's notice describes what follows April 15: real estate bills pass to the County Clerk, where a County Attorney fee of 20 percent, a clerk fee of 10 percent and interest of 1 percent monthly are charged, and an investor may buy the delinquency. A prior-year bill is paid at the clerk's counter, and the notice gives 606-564-3341 for the payoff.

Past-due reminders are never mailed. A bounced check costs $50 and returns the bill to unpaid. Cards work through the online link with a surcharge. If escrow or a new owner is responsible, pass the notice along at once.

sections.h2: How does a Mason County owner appeal a value through the Board of Appeals?
sections.html:
On the City of Maysville's board page, appeals begin at the PVA: talk the value over, review how it was figured, and take it to the Board of Appeals if nothing is resolved. The city seats an appointee on that board and lists the PVA, (606) 564-3700, as the contact.

The PVA's own page adds that appraisers see each property at least every four years and may measure a building's outside when nobody is home. In the statute, KRS 133.120 sets the order of steps, and KRS 133.030 puts the board's first meeting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Carry evidence of value and keep paying on your claimed figure until the board rules. A paid representative has to come from the professions the statute lists.

sections.h2: How much does the homestead exemption take off a Mason County bill?
sections.html: For 2025 and 2026 the exemption is $49,100, which trims a median $161,500 home to $112,400 of taxable value. Qualifying owners live in the house and are 65 or older, or totally disabled. The county website sends applicants to the PVA page, which also hosts a property search and a vehicle-tax exoneration affidavit. An approved age claim normally carries on while the same owner stays in the house; a buyer files afresh.

sections.h2: What happens with liens and the deed when a Mason County house sells?
sections.html:
The sheriff quotes this year's balance and the clerk quotes earlier years, and both come out of the sale proceeds. Under KRS 134.015(5) a delinquency lien can survive eleven years whoever holds title, so title agents insist on payoff.

Deeds are filed with the clerk at 27 West 3rd Street. The seller's transfer tax, fifty cents on each $500 of value under KRS 142.050, is $161.50 at the county median value. For electronic filing the clerk lists Hopdox, CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Confirm what each deed needs before sending it. Before you sign, use the property search on the county's PVA page to check that the owner name and mailing address on file match what the deed will say, and ask the PVA to correct any mismatch so the next tax bill reaches the right person.

faqs.q: What are the Mason County Sheriff's office hours?
faqs.a: Weekdays, opening at nine, at 120 West Third Street in Maysville. Call 606-564-3309. A drop box takes checks only.

faqs.q: What does a bounced check cost on a Mason County tax bill?
faqs.a: $50. The bill returns to unpaid status, and your repayment should follow the payment period printed on it.

faqs.q: Does the Mason County Sheriff mail past-due notices?
faqs.a: No. None is mailed, so watch the dates. Real estate bills still open after April 15 pass to the County Clerk with added fees.

faqs.q: Who sets tax rates in Mason County?
faqs.a: Elected bodies do: the fiscal court, city officials and school boards, among other taxing authorities. The PVA neither sets rates nor decides the total to be raised.

faqs.q: Can a Mason County bill be paid by card?
faqs.a: Yes, through the online link on the sheriff's site, where the card company adds a charge. Counter payments, mail and the check-only drop box also work.
